title: Pelvic MRI
also: MRI of the uterus and ovaries
what: Images of your pelvic organs in a magnetic field, with no radiation. They show the uterus, ovaries, bladder, rectum, and lymph nodes.
why: For pain low in the belly, fibroids and cysts, to clarify ultrasound findings, before surgery, and for follow-up.
duration: usually 30 to 45 minutes, longer with contrast; the report in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: A pacemaker, defibrillator, or other implant with electronics
Metal in your body: joint replacements, plates, clips on blood vessels, or shrapnel
If you are or might be pregnant
If you are afraid of closed spaces. Your doctor will suggest ways to help
If you have an IUD. Say which type

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 3 to 4 hours, so the bowel moves less. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: You are often asked to have a moderately full bladder: do not pee for an hour before. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Cycle
prepare.text: For women, certain cycle days are sometimes better. Ask the doctor who referred you.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off everything metal: jewelry, watches, hair clips, piercings. Leave your phone and cards in the locker.

bring: A creatinine test, if contrast will be used
steps: You change and leave everything metal in the locker
You lie on the table, and a soft coil pad is placed over the area
Sometimes a medicine is given so the bowel moves less
The machine knocks loudly. You get headphones or earplugs
Lie still. Staff talk to you over an intercom
You hold a call button and can call staff at any time
If contrast is used, it goes into a vein at the end
feel: It does not hurt, but it is loud and tight
Sometimes the area feels warm. That is normal
With contrast: a cool feeling in the vein
after: You can go back to your day right away
After contrast, drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
Take the report to your gynecologist, urologist, or colorectal specialist
red_flags: After contrast: itching, a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff right away or call emergency services

faq.q: Can I have a pelvic MRI during my period?
faq.a: Usually yes, but for some purposes other days are better. Ask your doctor.

faq.q: Do I need to remove my IUD?
faq.a: Usually not. Tell staff about it in advance.

faq.q: Can I have an MRI with fillings and crowns?
faq.a: Yes. Fillings and regular crowns are no problem. Tell staff about implants and prostheses in advance, and they will check.

reminders.text: Pelvic MRI soon. Usually no food for 3 to 4 hours. Take off everything metal.
